about: ANA Holdings is the Tokyo parent of All Nippon Airways, Japan's largest airline by passengers, flying domestic and international routes from Haneda and Narita, plus the low-cost carrier Peach. It carries roughly 50 million passengers a year with revenue around 2 trillion yen, and is a Star Alliance member. Listed in Tokyo (9202). ANA is a strong consumer brand across Japan and Asia, an official airline partner of the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and a sports sponsor.

wiki.title: All Nippon Airways
wiki.text: All Nippon Airways (ANA) is a Japanese airline headquartered in Minato, Tokyo. ANA operates services to over 100 both domestic and international destinations with its main hub at Haneda and Narita, both airports located in Tokyo. It is Japan's largest airline, ahead of its main rival Japan Airlines. As of March 2024, the airline has approximately 12,800 employees. The airline joined as a Star Alliance member in October 1999.

about: Mecachrome France is a Blagnac-based aerospace and motorsport engineering and manufacturing group that makes precision engine components, structural parts and complete racing engines. It produced Formula 1 engines for Renault, Honda and Mecachrome-branded supply, and builds parts for Airbus and Safran. Customers are aerospace and automotive OEMs. A B2B supplier with strong motorsport heritage, relevant to F1.

wiki.title: Mecachrome
wiki.text: Mecachrome SAS is a precision engineering company based in France that operates in the aerospace, motor racing, energy and defence sectors.

about: Macquarie Group, the Sydney-headquartered global financial services firm listed on the ASX (MQG), offering asset management, infrastructure investment, banking, commodities trading and advisory. Crunchbase links this entry to a San Francisco office and an aerospace-related financing of about $500 million in 2023. Customers are institutions, governments and corporates plus Australian retail banking clients. Operates in about 30 markets with some 20,000 staff. Large, highly recognisable financial brand in Australia, with sponsorships in arts and sport.
cb_desc: Macquarie is afinancial group that provides asset...

wiki.title: Macquarie Group
wiki.what: Australian investment bank and financial services company
wiki.text: Macquarie Group Limited, more commonly known as Macquarie Bank, is an Australian multinational investment banking and financial services group headquartered in Sydney and listed on the Australian Securities Exchange. The company employs more than 20,000 staff across four operating groups in 34 markets.

about: Voestalpine is an Austrian steel and technology group, based in Linz and listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange (VOE), with steel, high-performance metals, metal engineering and metal forming divisions, supplying the automotive, aerospace, rail, energy and construction industries worldwide. It employs about 50,000 people and has operations in around 50 countries. Revenue is from steel and engineered metal products. B2B industrial group, known in Austria, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Voestalpine
wiki.what: Austrian technology and capital goods group
wiki.text: Voestalpine AG – stylized as voestalpine – is an Austrian steel-based technology and capital goods group based in Linz, Austria. The company is active in steel, automotive, railway systems, profilform and tool steel industries. As of 2017, it is one of the few profitable steel companies in Europe.

about: EchoStar is a US satellite and wireless company based in Englewood, Colorado, and listed on Nasdaq (SATS). Its Hughes unit sells HughesNet satellite internet and network equipment for consumers, enterprises and governments. It merged with Dish Network in December 2023, adding Boost Mobile, Sling TV and a 5G network build, and in 2025 agreed to sell spectrum to AT&T and SpaceX. Founded by Charlie Ergen, it has revenue of around $15 billion. Boost Mobile and Sling are recognised US consumer brands.

wiki.title: EchoStar
wiki.text: EchoStar Corporation is an American telecommunications company, specializing in satellite communication, wireless telecommunications, and internet services. Echostar also provides multichannel video programming and mobile services through its subsidiaries: Dish Network, Boost Mobile, Sling TV, EchoStar Mobile, and Hughes Network Systems.

about: Aircraft engine and systems maker based in Cincinnati, Ohio, which was the aviation division of General Electric and became GE Aerospace in 2024 when GE spun off its other businesses. It makes jet engines including the CFM LEAP (with Safran), GE9X and GEnx, plus avionics, and earns revenue from engine sales and long-term service contracts. Customers are airlines, aircraft makers and militaries. Large B2B brand with high awareness in aviation and some consumer familiarity from the GE name.

wiki.title: GE Aerospace
wiki.text: General Electric Company is an American aircraft engine supplier that is headquartered in Evendale, Ohio, outside Cincinnati. It is the legal successor to the original General Electric Company founded in 1892, which split into three separate companies between November 2021 and April 2024, adopting the trade name GE Aerospace after divesting its healthcare and energy divisions.

about: One of the world's largest defence and aerospace contractors, with around 110,000 employees and revenue above 40 billion dollars. It builds Gulfstream business jets, Electric Boat nuclear submarines, Abrams tanks and Stryker vehicles, naval ships through Bath Iron Works and NASSCO, and runs GDIT, an IT services business. Customers are the US Department of Defense, allied governments and business-jet owners. Founded 1952, NYSE: GD. Strong B2B and government brand, with Gulfstream the most visible luxury consumer-adjacent name.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 2010: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: General Dynamics
wiki.text: General Dynamics Corporation (GD) is an American industrial and technology company based in Reston, Virginia. It is primarily a developer and producer of advanced military equipment of a wide variety, such as nuclear submarines, main battle tanks, and armoured fighting vehicles. It is also the manufacturer of the civilian aviation Gulfstream business jets and a provider of information technology services. The company is the 3rd largest of the top 100 contractors of the U.S. federal government; it receives over 3% of total spending by the federal government of the United States on contractors.

about: Hainan Airlines is a Chinese full-service airline founded in 1993 and based on Hainan island, a subsidiary of HNA group, now flagship of Hainan Airlines Holding under a 2021 restructuring led by Liaoning Fangda. Flies domestic and international routes from Haikou, Beijing and elsewhere, serving leisure and business travellers. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600221). Well-known Chinese carrier with a Skytrax five-star rating history.
cb_desc: Hainan Airlines is a China- based airline and subsidiary of...

wiki.title: Hainan Airlines
wiki.text: Hainan Airlines is an airline headquartered in Haikou, Hainan, China. It is the largest civilian-run Chinese air transport company, making it the fourth-largest airline in terms of fleet size in the People's Republic of China, and the tenth-largest airline in Asia in terms of passengers carried. It operates scheduled domestic and international services on 500 routes from Hainan and various locations on the mainland, as well as charter services. Its main base is located at Haikou Meilan International Airport, with hubs at Beijing-Capital, Chongqing, Shenzhen and Xi'an, along with several focus cities.

about: Alaska Airlines is a major US carrier, the fifth largest after merging Hawaiian Airlines in 2024, flying passengers and cargo from hubs in Seattle, Portland, Anchorage, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Honolulu. Operates a fleet of Boeing 737s plus regional partners, with revenue near 14 billion dollars. Headquartered in Seattle (SeaTac), founded 1932. Subsidiary of Alaska Air Group, listed on the New York Stock Exchange (ALK). Strong West Coast consumer brand, with college and pro sports partnerships.

wiki.title: Alaska Airlines
wiki.text: Alaska Airlines is a major airline in the United States headquartered in SeaTac, Washington, within the Seattle metropolitan area. It is the fifth-largest airline in North America when measured by scheduled passengers carried, as of 2024. Alaska, together with its regional partners Horizon Air and SkyWest Airlines, operates a route network primarily focused on connecting cities along the West Coast of the United States to over 100 destinations in the contiguous United States, North America, Asia, Oceania, and Europe.

about: American Airlines is the world's largest airline by fleet size and passengers, flying to over 350 destinations from hubs in Dallas-Fort Worth, Charlotte, Chicago, Miami, Philadelphia and Phoenix, and a member of Oneworld. Revenue near 54 billion dollars, with about 130,000 employees. Headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas; formed 1930. Listed on Nasdaq (AAL). Has restructured after the 2013 US Airways merger. Household US consumer brand with long-standing sports naming rights (American Airlines Center and Arena).

wiki.title: American Airlines
wiki.text: American Airlines, Inc. is a major airline in the United States headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, within the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex. It is the largest airline in the world in terms of passengers carried and daily flights. American, along with its regional subsidiaries and contractors operating under the brand name American Eagle, operates an extensive international and domestic network with almost 6,800 flights per day to nearly 350 destinations in 48 countries. The airline is also a founding member of Oneworld alliance, one of the world's three major airline alliances.

about: Southwest Airlines is a US low-cost carrier, the largest domestic carrier by passengers, flying a Boeing 737 fleet to more than 100 destinations, historically with open seating and free checked bags (changed in 2025). Revenue near 28 billion dollars. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas; founded 1967. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (LUV). Activist investor Elliott pressed changes in 2024. Well known US consumer brand with extensive sports partnerships.

wiki.title: Southwest Airlines
wiki.text: Southwest Airlines is a low-cost airline in the United States. It is headquartered in the Love Field neighborhood of Dallas, Texas. It is the fourth-largest airline in North America when measured by passengers carried, as of 2024. With its all-Boeing 737 fleet, Southwest serves over 100 destinations in 42 states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico, and ten other countries and territories near the southern United States in the Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean Sea regions: Aruba, the Bahamas, Belize, the Cayman Islands, Costa Rica, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Jamaica, and Turks and Caicos Islands.

about: United Airlines is one of the largest US carriers, flying passengers and cargo to more than 300 destinations from hubs in Chicago, Newark, Houston, Denver, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Washington, as a Star Alliance member with the MileagePlus loyalty programme. Revenue near 57 billion dollars and about 100,000 employees. Headquartered in Chicago; part of United Airlines Holdings, listed on Nasdaq (UAL). Major US consumer brand with extensive sports and entertainment sponsorships.

wiki.title: United Airlines
wiki.text: United Airlines, Inc. is a major airline in the United States headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. It operates an extensive domestic and international route network across the United States and to destinations on six continents. Regional service is provided by independent carriers operating under the United Express brand, and the Star Alliance, of which United was one of the five founding airlines, extends its network throughout the world.

about: International Airlines Group (IAG) is the parent of British Airways, Iberia, Vueling, Aer Lingus, Level and the loyalty scheme Avios, flying to more than 200 destinations and carrying over 100 million passengers a year. Revenue near 33 billion euros. Headquartered in London (with Madrid origins), formed 2011. Listed in London and Madrid (IAG). Strong airline brands with substantial sponsorships, such as British Airways' links to sport.

wiki.title: International Airlines Group
wiki.text: International Consolidated Airlines Group S.A., trading as International Airlines Group and usually shortened to IAG, is an Anglo-Spanish multinational airline holding company with its registered office in Madrid, Spain, and its corporate headquarters in London, England. It was formed in January 2011 after a merger agreement between British Airways and Iberia, the flag carriers of the United Kingdom and Spain respectively, when both became wholly owned subsidiaries of IAG. British Airways shareholders were given 55% of the shares in the new company.

about: AerCap is the world's largest aircraft lessor, headquartered in Dublin, with owned and managed assets of aircraft, engines and helicopters worth tens of billions of dollars. It leases planes to about 300 airlines worldwide, earning rental income and sale gains, and completed its purchase of GE Capital Aviation Services in 2021. Listed on the NYSE (AER) and led by Aengus Kelly. B2B financier, known in aviation, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: AerCap
wiki.text: AerCap Holdings N.V. is an Irish aviation leasing company based in Dublin, Ireland, with its registered office based in Amsterdam, Netherlands. AerCap is listed on the NYSE with the ticker 'AER'. It became the largest aviation leasing company in the world following the acquisition of ILFC in 2014, and GECAS from GE in 2021, for over $30 billion.

about: LATAM Airlines Group is Latin America's largest airline group, headquartered in Santiago, Chile, with affiliates in Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador and Argentina, flying to over 140 destinations plus a cargo arm. It carries over 70 million passengers a year, with annual revenue near $13bn, and emerged from US Chapter 11 in 2022. Listed on the Santiago stock exchange (LTM) and NYSE ADRs. Strong regional consumer brand with sponsorship in sports across Latin America and international football.

wiki.title: LATAM Airlines
wiki.text: LATAM Airlines is a Chilean multinational airline headquartered in Santiago, Chile. It is the largest airline holding company in Latin America with subsidiaries in Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay and Peru.

about: DSV is a Danish global transport and logistics company, headquartered in Hedehusene, near Copenhagen, offering air and sea freight, road transport and contract logistics in about 80 countries. After buying DB Schenker in 2025 for about DKK 106bn, it has more than 150,000 employees, with revenue above DKK 200bn. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (DSV). B2B logistics firm with strong industry reputation, and its trucks and containers carry the brand, but consumers rarely know it.

wiki.title: DSV (company)
wiki.text: DSV A/S is a Danish transport and logistics company offering global transport services by road, air, sea and train. Since its foundation in 1976 by nine independent Danish hauliers, the company expanded predominantly through a series of competitor acquisitions.

about: Heathrow Airport Holdings owns and operates London Heathrow, Britain's busiest airport and one of the world's largest hubs, handling about 83 million passengers a year across four terminals. It earns aeronautical charges from airlines and retail, parking and property revenue. Owned by a consortium led by Ferrovial, Qatar Investment Authority, Canada's CDPQ and GIC, Alinda, USS and others, with Ferrovial reducing its stake. Private. Hugely recognised consumer-facing brand, with premium sponsorship opportunities.

wiki.title: Heathrow Airport Holdings
wiki.what: Company based in the United Kingdom
wiki.text: Heathrow Airport Holdings is a company that operates and manages Heathrow Airport based in London, England. It was formed by the privatisation of the British Airports Authority as BAA plc as part of Margaret Thatcher's privatisation of government-owned assets, and was once a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index.

about: Vietnam Airlines is Vietnam's state-owned flag carrier, based in Hanoi, with a fleet of Airbus and Boeing aircraft (including A350 and 787) flying to over 20 countries and many domestic routes under the Golden Lotus brand, and a member of SkyTeam. It carries over 20 million passengers a year, with Vietnam Airlines Group also owning Pacific Airlines and VASCO. Majority-owned by the government through SCIC and listed on the Vietnamese UPCoM market (HVN). Strongly recognised by Vietnamese consumers, with sports and event sponsorships.

wiki.title: Vietnam Airlines
wiki.text: Vietnam Airlines is the flag carrier of Vietnam. The airline was founded in 1956 and later established as a state-owned enterprise in April 1989. Vietnam Airlines is headquartered in Long Biên district, Hanoi, with hubs at Noi Bai International Airport in Hanoi and Tan Son Nhat International Airport in Ho Chi Minh City. The airline flies 117 routes across 19 countries, excluding codeshared services.

about: gategroup is a Swiss airline catering and onboard services company, based in Glattbrugg near Zurich, supplying meals, retail products, equipment and lounges to airlines worldwide through more than 190 units in about 60 countries. It was acquired by RRJ Capital in 2016 and later had HNA and Temasek links, restructured and sold to new owners. Private. B2B with little consumer brand recognition, though its products are used on airlines passengers' flights.

wiki.title: Gategroup
wiki.what: Swiss company providing food-related services to the travel industry
wiki.text: Gategroup is a Swiss company providing services to the travel industry, including catering, onboard retail, food service provisioning, and food logistics. Gategroup operates more than 200 facilities in over 60 countries. Its head office is in Glattbrugg, Switzerland, near Zurich Airport.

about: Gol Linhas Aereas (Gol Transportes Aereos) is a Brazilian low-cost airline based in Sao Paulo, flying a Boeing 737 fleet on domestic and South American routes, with more than 30 million passengers a year. It filed for US Chapter 11 in January 2024 and emerged in June 2025 with Abra Group as its parent, after which it delisted from the NYSE and B3. Revenue is near BRL 20bn. Well-known Brazilian consumer airline brand, with football and sports sponsorship history.

wiki.title: Gol Linhas Aéreas
wiki.text: GOL Linhas Aéreas S.A is a Brazilian low cost airline based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. According to the National Civil Aviation Agency of Brazil (ANAC), between January and December 2019, GOL had 37.7% of the domestic and 3.8% of the international market shares in terms of passenger-kilometers flown, making it the largest domestic and third largest international airline in Brazil.

about: Virgin Atlantic Airways is a British long-haul airline based in Crawley, West Sussex, flying from London Heathrow, Gatwick and Manchester to North America, the Caribbean, Africa, India and Asia, with about 40 aircraft and over 5 million passengers a year. Delta Air Lines holds 49 percent, Virgin Group 51 percent, and the airline is private. It emerged from a 2020 rescue package. Strong consumer brand with the Virgin name, and sponsorship and brand tie-ins.

wiki.title: Virgin Atlantic
wiki.text: Virgin Atlantic, a trading name of Virgin Atlantic Airways Limited and Virgin Atlantic International Limited, is a British airline with its head office in Crawley, West Sussex, England. The airline was established in 1984 as British Atlantic Airways, and was originally planned by its co-founders Randolph Fields and Alan Hellary to fly between London and the Falkland Islands. Soon after changing the name to Virgin Atlantic Airways, Fields sold his shares in the company to Richard Branson in return for unlimited free travel. Its maiden flight from London–Gatwick to Newark took place on 22 June 1984.

about: Grupo Aeromexico is Mexico's flag-carrier airline group based in Mexico City, flying domestic and international routes to the US, Latin America, Europe and Asia from its Mexico City hub, and a founding member of the SkyTeam alliance. It carries about 25 million passengers a year, with a fleet of roughly 150 aircraft. Delta Air Lines owns a stake of around 20 percent. It returned to the Mexican exchange and the NYSE in 2025 (AEROMEX). High consumer brand awareness in Mexico.

wiki.title: Grupo Aeroméxico
wiki.text: Grupo Aeroméxico S.A.B. de C.V. is an airline holding company headquartered in Mexico City. Grupo Aeroméxico owns and operates Aeroméxico, the principal airline of Mexico.

about: Delta Air Lines is a major US airline headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia and listed on the NYSE (DAL). It operates a hub-and-spoke network to over 275 destinations on six continents, carrying over 200 million passengers a year with a fleet of roughly 1,000 aircraft and revenue of about 60 billion dollars. It also has a loyalty programme (SkyMiles), cargo and MRO services, and owns a refinery. Founded 1925. Very strong consumer brand, SkyTeam founding member, and an active sports marketer.

wiki.title: Delta Air Lines
wiki.text: Delta Air Lines, Inc. is a major airline in the United States headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, operating nine hubs, with Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport being its largest in terms of total passengers and number of departures. With its regional subsidiaries and contractors operating under the brand name Delta Connection, Delta has over 5,400 flights daily and serves 325 destinations in 52 countries on six continents.

about: Ryanair is Europe's largest low-cost airline group by passengers, headquartered in Dublin and listed on Euronext Dublin and Nasdaq (RYAAY). It flies a fleet of about 600 Boeing 737s to over 230 airports in 37 countries, carrying more than 200 million passengers a year with revenue near 14 billion euros. Group airlines include Buzz, Malta Air and Lauda Europe. Founded 1984 and led by Michael O'Leary. Very high consumer recognition, known for aggressive, humorous advertising.

wiki.title: Ryanair
wiki.text: Ryanair is an Irish ultra-low-cost airline headquartered in Swords, County Dublin, Ireland. It is the largest airline in Europe by scheduled passengers carried, fleet size, and total flights. Globally, it is the largest airline by international passengers carried, the third-largest by market capitalisation behind Delta Air Lines and United Airlines, and the fifth-most profitable by net income. In 2025, the company sold 208 million airline tickets, averaging €70 in total revenue against €62 in costs per ticket sold. It is widely considered to be the cheapest airline operating in Europe.

about: Azerbaijan Airlines (AZAL) is the national flag carrier of Azerbaijan, headquartered in Baku and owned by the state. It flies Airbus, Boeing and Embraer aircraft to destinations in Europe, Asia and the Middle East, and is the main carrier at Baku's Heydar Aliyev airport. Founded in 1992 from the Soviet-era Aeroflot division. One of its aircraft crashed near Aktau, Kazakhstan, in December 2024. Established national brand in a country that hosts an F1 race at Baku.

wiki.title: Azerbaijan Airlines
wiki.what: Flag carrier and largest airline of Azerbaijan
wiki.text: Azerbaijan Airlines, known in short as AZAL, is the designated flag carrier and largest airline of Azerbaijan. Based in Baku, adjacent to Heydar Aliyev International Airport, the carrier operates to destinations across Asia, the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS), and Europe.

about: Italian flag carrier airline based at Rome Fiumicino, created in 2021 as successor to Alitalia and owned by the Italian Treasury with Lufthansa Group taking a minority stake in 2025. Flies about 80 aircraft to Europe, the Americas and Asia. Strong Italian consumer brand with sports sponsorship, including the Italian national team. ITA has a fleet of about 90 aircraft and over 5,000 employees, and has been backed by the Italian Treasury.

wiki.title: ITA Airways
wiki.text: ITA Airways, , is the flag carrier of Italy. It is owned by the government of Italy, via the Ministry of Economy and Finance, and Lufthansa Group.

about: New Saudi flag carrier based in Riyadh, owned by the Public Investment Fund and launched in 2023, with orders for Boeing 787 and Airbus A321neo aircraft and first commercial flights in 2025-26. Targets premium international travellers. New consumer brand with sports sponsorship, including the shirt of Atletico Madrid. The airline plans to operate from King Salman International Airport and has booked aircraft from Boeing and Airbus.

wiki.title: Riyadh Air
wiki.text: Riyadh Air is the second flag carrier of Saudi Arabia after Saudia, based in Riyadh. The airline's main hub is at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, and is aimed at the world market, operating domestic and internationally scheduled flights to over 100 destinations in six continents. The fleet will consist of 4 aircraft types, 60 Airbus A321neo, 31 Airbus A350-1000, 47 Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, and 20 Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner aircraft, with options for more.

about: Shanghai-based flag carrier airline, one of China's big three, flying domestic and international routes, member of SkyTeam, state-owned and listed in Shanghai, Hong Kong and NYSE. Revenue about CNY 140 billion. Strong consumer brand in China. Part of China Eastern Air Holdings, with a fleet of over 700 aircraft. Hub airports in Shanghai Pudong and Hongqiao. Strong consumer brand across China.

wiki.title: China Eastern Airlines
wiki.text: China Eastern Airlines is a major airline in China, headquartered in Minhang, Shanghai. It is one of the three major airlines in the country, along with Air China and China Southern Airlines.

about: Ethiopian Airlines is Ethiopia's state-owned flag carrier and Africa's largest airline by fleet and revenue, headquartered in Addis Ababa with a hub at Bole International Airport, flying to over 140 destinations worldwide. It is a Star Alliance member and operates Boeing and Airbus fleets, with cargo, MRO and training businesses. Funding shown is about 1.1 billion dollars. Strong brand across Africa, and sponsors of sport and events.

wiki.title: Ethiopian Airlines
wiki.text: Ethiopian Airlines, formerly Ethiopian Air Lines (EAL), is the flag carrier of Ethiopia, and is wholly owned by the country's government. EAL was founded on 21 December 1945 and commenced operations on 8 April 1946, expanding to international flights in 1951. The firm became a share company in 1965 and changed its name from Ethiopian Air Lines to Ethiopian Airlines.

about: Malaysian low-cost airline brand founded in 2001 by Tony Fernandes, now under the Capital A group, flying across Asia with about 200 aircraft. Large following, sponsor of football and motorsport. Tony Fernandes and Kamarudin Meranun bought the airline in 2001 for a token sum. Fernandes also ran the Caterham Formula 1 team and the airline sponsored F1 outfits in that period. The AirAsia group, now Capital A, also has the AirAsia Move super-app. Strong consumer brand across Southeast Asia.

wiki.title: AirAsia
wiki.text: AirAsia Group Berhad, operating as AirAsia, is a Malaysian multinational low-cost airline headquartered near Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Established in 1993 and commencing operations in 1996, the airline is the largest in Malaysia by fleet size and destinations. It operates scheduled domestic and international flights to over 166 destinations across 25 countries. Its primary hub is Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), where it operates from Terminal 2, the low-cost carrier terminal.

about: Hong Kong's flagship airline, Cathay Pacific, flying to over 80 destinations with a hub at Hong Kong International Airport. Owned by Swire, Air China and Qatar Airways; listed on HKEX (293). Cathay was founded in 1946, and Swire holds roughly 45 percent. It also runs HK Express, bought in 2019, and cargo airline Air Hong Kong. It sponsors the Hong Kong Sevens. High-visibility consumer brand and prior sports sponsor including rugby sevens.

wiki.title: Cathay Pacific
wiki.text: Cathay Pacific Airways Limited, or simply Cathay Pacific, is the flag carrier of Hong Kong, with its head office and main hub located at Hong Kong International Airport. The airline's operations and its subsidiaries have scheduled passenger and cargo services to more than 190 destinations and more than 60 countries worldwide including codeshares and joint ventures.

about: EasyJet is a British low-cost airline founded in 1995 by Stelios Haji-Ioannou and headquartered at London Luton Airport. It operates a fleet of around 350 Airbus A320 family aircraft to over 150 airports in more than 35 countries, carrying roughly 90 million passengers a year, and sells package holidays via easyJet holidays. Revenue is about 9 billion pounds. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (EZJ) and FTSE 100 member. A well-known European consumer brand with high retail awareness.

wiki.title: EasyJet
wiki.text: EasyJet plc is a British low-cost airline and package holiday multinational group headquartered at Luton Airport. It operates domestic and international scheduled services on 927 routes in more than 34 countries via its affiliate airlines EasyJet UK, EasyJet Switzerland and EasyJet Europe. It also operates as a package holiday provider to more than 100 destinations across Europe and North Africa through its subsidiary EasyJet Holidays Limited. The company employs around 13,000 people, based throughout Europe but mainly in the UK. EasyJet plc is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index.

about: China Southern Airlines is one of China's three largest state-owned airlines, headquartered in Guangzhou, with a fleet of around 900 aircraft serving more than 200 destinations. It flies from hubs in Guangzhou and Beijing Daxing, and is a member of the SkyTeam alliance. Revenue is above 20 billion dollars and it carries more than 100 million passengers a year. Controlled by China Southern Air Holding, a state-owned enterprise, and listed in Shanghai (600029), Hong Kong (1055) and NYSE (ZNH). Strong consumer brand in China and Asia.

wiki.title: China Southern Airlines
wiki.text: China Southern Airlines is a major airline in China, headquartered in Guangzhou, Guangdong. It is one of the three major airlines in the country, along with Air China and China Eastern Airlines.

about: Cruise company operating Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea, plus a stake in TUI Cruises, with more than 65 ships and private destinations such as Perfect Day at CocoCay. Sells cruise vacations to consumers through travel agents and direct bookings, with revenue near 16 billion dollars. Headquartered in Miami, Florida; founded 1968. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (RCL). Strong consumer brands in the US and Europe, with a history of sports sponsorship and marketing partnerships.

wiki.title: Royal Caribbean Group
wiki.what: Cruise holding company headquartered in Miami, Florida
wiki.text: Royal Caribbean Group, formerly known as Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd., is a cruise holding company headquartered in Miami, Florida, United States and incorporated in Liberia. It is the world's second-largest cruise line operator, after Carnival Corporation & plc. As of September 2025, Royal Caribbean Group fully owns three cruise lines: Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises, and Silversea Cruises. It also holds a 50% stake in TUI Cruises, which operates Mein Schiff and Hapag-Lloyd Cruises, with the Group's global fleet consisting of 71 ships.

about: Online marketplace for short-term home rentals and experiences, connecting hosts with travellers in more than 220 countries and regions, with millions of listings. Earns service fees from guests and hosts, with revenue around 12 billion dollars and over 4 billion guest arrivals since founding. Headquartered in San Francisco; founded 2008. Listed on Nasdaq (ABNB) since its 2020 IPO. Globally recognised consumer brand, and a past Olympic and Paralympic sponsor and partner of major sports and events.

wiki.title: Airbnb
wiki.what: Online platform for short-term housing rentals
wiki.text: Airbnb, Inc. is an American company operating an online marketplace for short-and-long-term homestays, experiences and services in various countries and regions. It acts as a broker and charges a commission from each booking. Airbnb was founded in 2008 by Brian Chesky, Nathan Blecharczyk, and Joe Gebbia.

about: Global travel retail and food service group, created by the 2023 merger of Dufry and Autogrill, operating duty-free and convenience shops (Dufry, Hudson, Duty Free) and restaurants in airports, railway stations, motorway services and cruise ships in 70 countries. Revenue near 14 billion Swiss francs from travelling consumers. Headquartered in Basel. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (AVOL). Visible to travellers as airport retail brands, with limited stand-alone brand awareness.

wiki.title: Avolta
wiki.text: Avolta AG is a Swiss-based travel retailer that operates duty-free and duty-paid shops and convenience stores in airports, cruise lines, seaports, railway stations, and central tourist areas. The company, headquartered in Basel, employs almost 75,000 people and operates in over 75 countries worldwide. It is publicly traded on the SIX Swiss Exchange.

about: Online travel group operating Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Travelocity, Wotif and the B2B Expedia Partner Solutions, selling flights, hotels, vacation rentals and packages to travellers worldwide. Earns commissions and advertising, with gross bookings above 100 billion dollars and revenue near 13 billion dollars. Headquartered in Seattle, Washington; spun out of Microsoft in 1996. Listed on Nasdaq (EXPE), with Liberty Expedia and Barry Diller's family as major shareholders. Widely known consumer travel brands with marketing and sports partnerships.

wiki.title: Expedia Group
wiki.text: Expedia Group, Inc. is an American travel technology company that owns and operates travel fare aggregators and travel metasearch engines, including Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Travelocity, Hotwire.com, Orbitz, Ebookers, CheapTickets, CarRentals.com, Expedia Cruises, Wotif, and Trivago. Over 3.5 million lodging facilities and flights on over 500 airlines are bookable on the company's websites. It has 16,500 employees, and its headquarters are located in Seattle, Washington.

wiki.title: Expedia
wiki.what: Online travel agency and metasearch engine
wiki.text: Expedia Inc. is an American online travel agency owned by Expedia Group, which is headquartered in Seattle, Washington. When Microsoft Corporation launched Expedia on the Microsoft Network in October 1996, it was the first online travel service to be offered by a major technology company, allowing consumers to make air, car, and hotel reservations online and to browse a library of multimedia travel guides. Expedia was founded on October 22, 1996, inside Microsoft in Redmond, Washington, led by Richard (Rich) Barton and a small team who saw an opportunity to bring transparent airfare, hotel, and car booking directly to consumers without travel

about: Car rental company operating Hertz, Dollar and Thrifty brands at airports and city locations in North America, Europe and elsewhere, and renting to leisure and business travellers plus Firefly, and it has used EVs including Tesla in its fleet. Revenue near 8 billion dollars. Headquartered in Estero, Florida; founded 1918. Listed on Nasdaq (HTZ), emerged from 2021 bankruptcy with Knighthead and Certares as large holders. Major consumer travel brand with a long motorsport and sports marketing record.

wiki.title: Hertz
wiki.text: The hertz is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event per second. The hertz is an SI derived unit whose formal expression in terms of SI base units is 1/s or s−1, meaning that one hertz is one per second or the reciprocal of one second. It is used only in the case of periodic events. It is named after Heinrich Rudolf Hertz (1857–1894), the first person to provide conclusive proof of the existence of electromagnetic waves. For high frequencies, the unit is commonly expressed in multiples: kilohertz (kHz), megahertz (MHz), gigahertz (GHz), terahertz (THz).

wiki.title: Hertz Global Holdings
wiki.text: Hertz Global Holdings, Inc., is an American car rental company based in Estero, Florida. The company operates its namesake Hertz brand, along with the brands Dollar Rent A Car, Firefly Car Rental, and Thrifty Car Rental.

about: World's largest cruise company, operating Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, P&O Cruises, Cunard, Costa Cruises and AIDA with around 90 ships. Sells cruise holidays to millions of consumers a year, with revenue near 25 billion dollars. Headquartered in Miami, Florida, with Carnival plc in the UK; founded 1972. Dual listed on the New York Stock Exchange (CCL) and London (CCL). Very strong consumer brands with sports and entertainment sponsorships.

wiki.title: Carnival Corporation
wiki.text: Carnival Corporation Ltd. is a Bermuda-domiciled American cruise line operator that owns more than 90 vessels across eight brands. Carnival is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, and is a component of the S&P 500 index. From 2003 to May 7, 2026, Carnival was a dual-listed company, consisting of U.S.-based and British corporations collectively known as Carnival Corporation & plc.

about: Indian hospitality technology company that signs up independent hotels and homes into a branded network (OYO Rooms, OYO Townhouse, Belvilla in Europe, and Oravel Stays), operating mainly in India, Southeast Asia, Europe and the US. Earns commissions and revenue share from hotels, with a large chain presence. Headquartered in Gurugram; founded 2013 by Ritesh Agarwal. Private (parent PRISM) backed by SoftBank, which cut its valuation sharply; a listing was planned. Widely recognised budget hotel brand in India.

Booking Holdings is the world's largest online travel company, headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut. Its brands include Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, offering hotel and flight reservations, car rentals and restaurant bookings, earning commissions and advertising fees. Revenue is above $23bn with about 24,000 employees, serving travellers in 200+ countries. Listed on Nasdaq (BKNG). Booking.com is a major consumer brand with huge advertising spend, and the group has used sports sponsorship, including Booking.com's tie-ups in football and with Formula 1 rival series.

wiki.title: Booking Holdings
wiki.text: Booking Holdings Inc. is an American travel technology company based in Norwalk, Connecticut, that owns and operates several travel fare aggregators and travel fare metasearch engines including namesake and flagship Booking.com, Priceline.com, Agoda, Kayak, Cheapflights, Rentalcars.com, Momondo, and OpenTable. It operates websites in about 40 languages and 200 countries.

about: Sandals Resorts International is a luxury all-inclusive resort operator headquartered in Montego Bay, Jamaica, and founded by Gordon Butch Stewart in 1981. It runs Sandals (couples-focused) and Beaches (family-focused) resorts across the Caribbean in Jamaica, Saint Lucia, Antigua, Barbados, Grenada, the Bahamas and elsewhere. Guests are mostly North American and UK vacationers, with revenue from room rates, packages and add-ons. Privately owned by the Stewart family, now run by Adam Stewart. Strong consumer brand recognition in the US and UK through heavy advertising.

wiki.title: Sandals Resorts
wiki.text: Sandals Resorts is a Jamaican operator of all-inclusive couples resorts in the Caribbean. The company is a part of Sandals Resorts International (SRI), which also operates Beaches Resorts, Fowl Cay Resort, and several private villas. Founded by Jamaican-born entrepreneur Gordon "Butch" Stewart in 1981, SRI is based in Montego Bay, Jamaica and is responsible for development, service standards, training, and day-to-day operations of the resorts.

about: Abercrombie and Kent is a global luxury travel company, founded in 1962 by Geoffrey Kent in Kenya, offering private journeys, safaris, cruises and small-group tours in over 100 countries, with offices worldwide and a US base in Downers Grove, Illinois. Customers are affluent leisure travellers, earning revenue from tour and trip bookings. Privately held, with investors including Dubai-based and US capital. A premium travel brand with strong awareness among high-net-worth travellers.

wiki.title: Geoffrey Kent
wiki.what: Founder of luxury travel firm Abercrombie & Kent
wiki.text: Geoffrey JW Kent is the Founder and Chairman Emeritus of Abercrombie & Kent, an international luxury and adventure travel company. He is credited with introducing the first luxury photographic African safari in 1962.

about: American Express Global Business Travel (Amex GBT) is a New York corporate travel management company providing booking tools, expense management and meetings services to businesses, with acquisition of CWT in 2025. It serves thousands of corporate clients in over 140 countries and earns transaction fees. Listed on the NYSE (GBTG) since a 2022 SPAC, with American Express, Qatar Investment Authority and Juweel as major holders. B2B, well known to travel buyers, with the Amex-linked brand partly visible.

wiki.title: American Express Global Business Travel
wiki.text: Global Business Travel Group, Inc. is a multinational travel management company headquartered in New York City. Amex GBT has 18,000 employees in more than 140 countries. American Express holds a minority interest in Amex GBT, but the travel company operates as a separate entity from the financial services group.

about: Transat A.T. is a Montreal-based integrated Canadian tour operator and airline group, selling vacation packages, flights and hotel stays to destinations in the Caribbean, Europe and Mexico under Air Transat and the Transat travel brand, with offices in Canada, France and the UK. Revenue is about C$2.9bn. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TRZ). Strong Canadian consumer travel brand, with Air Transat well known in Quebec and across Canada.

wiki.title: Transat A.T.
wiki.text: Transat A.T. Inc. is an international, vertically integrated tour operator with nearly 20 business units in 8 countries. The company is headquartered in Montreal, Quebec, Canada.

about: Travelport is a global travel technology company, based in Langley, Berkshire, whose distribution platform connects airlines, hotels and car rental firms to travel agencies and online booking sites. It earns transaction fees from bookings, and in 2019 was taken private by Siris Capital and Elliott. The company later combined with others and carries a sizeable debt load. Private. B2B travel platform, with no consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Travelport
wiki.what: Smallest, by revenue, of the top three global distribution systems
wiki.text: Travelport Worldwide Ltd. provides distribution, technology, and payment solutions for the travel and tourism industry. It is the smallest, by revenue, of the top three global distribution systems (GDS) after Amadeus IT Group and Sabre Corporation.

about: Las Vegas Sands is a Las Vegas-based resort developer and operator of integrated casino resorts. It sold its Las Vegas properties, the Venetian and Palazzo, in 2022 and now focuses on Singapore (Marina Bay Sands) and Macau (The Venetian Macao, The Londoner, The Parisian). Revenue is around $11bn, earned from gaming, hotel, retail, convention and entertainment. Listed on the NYSE (LVS), controlled by the Adelson family. Marina Bay Sands is an iconic Singapore landmark with strong travel brand visibility.

wiki.title: Las Vegas Sands
wiki.text: Las Vegas Sands Corp. is an American casino and resort company with corporate headquarters in Las Vegas, Nevada. It was founded by Sheldon G. Adelson and his partners out of the Sands Hotel and Casino on the Las Vegas Strip. The Sands was demolished and redeveloped as The Venetian, opening in 1999. An adjacent resort, The Palazzo, opened in 2007. Both resorts were sold in 2022.

about: Melco Resorts and Entertainment is a Hong Kong-based casino resort developer and operator with properties in Macau (City of Dreams, Studio City, Altira), Manila (City of Dreams Manila) and Cyprus. Led by Lawrence Ho, it earns from gaming, rooms, dining, entertainment and retail, with revenue near US$4.5bn. Listed on Nasdaq (MLCO) and Hong Kong (6883). Strong consumer brand in Asian gaming and tourism, and a notable sponsor with a Macau Grand Prix link.

wiki.title: Melco Resorts & Entertainment
wiki.what: Integrated resorts company based in Hong Kong
wiki.text: Melco Resorts & Entertainment Limited is a developer, owner and operator of integrated resorts with entertainment and casino gaming facilities in Asia and Europe. Based in Hong Kong, the company is listed on the NASDAQ. Originally known as Melco Crown Entertainment, Melco Resorts was founded in 2004 as a joint venture between Melco International and Crown Limited. Melco Crown became Melco Resorts & Entertainment in May 2017 and currently operates as a subsidiary of Melco International. Melco Resorts owns a number of integrated casino resorts, having launched Altira Macau in 2007, City of Dreams Macau in 2009, City of Dreams Manila in 2015, St

about: Tripadvisor is a Needham, Massachusetts travel platform where users read reviews and book hotels, tours, restaurants (via TheFork) and experiences, with brands including Viator, TheFork and Tripadvisor itself. It earns commissions and advertising and has revenue of about $1.8bn. Listed on Nasdaq (TRIP), with Liberty TripAdvisor merged in 2025. Very high consumer awareness in travel, with a community of reviewers and advertising partnerships.

wiki.title: Tripadvisor
wiki.text: Tripadvisor is an American company that operates online travel agencies, comparison shopping websites, and mobile apps with user-generated content.

about: Fosun Tourism Group is a Shanghai-based Chinese resort and travel group owned by Fosun International, operating Club Med (acquired 2015), Atlantis Sanya, Thomas Cook brand assets in some markets and Foliday and Lijiang resorts. It earns room, tour and resort revenue. It listed in Hong Kong in 2018 (1992) and was later delisted from the Hong Kong market after Fosun's takeover. Club Med is a notable global leisure brand, popular in Europe and Asia.

Viking Cruises is a Basel, Switzerland-based cruise line founded by Torstein Hagen in 1997, operating river and ocean cruises and expedition ships to Europe, Asia, Egypt and the Americas under Viking River, Viking Ocean and Viking Expeditions. It targets affluent older travellers, sells directly, and has fleets of over 90 ships. It listed on the NYSE in 2024 (VIK). Strong brand recognition in the US and UK, known for sponsoring Masterpiece Theatre on PBS.

wiki.title: Viking (cruise line)
wiki.text: Viking is a cruise line providing river, ocean, and expedition cruises. Its operating headquarters are in Basel, Switzerland, and its marketing headquarters are in Los Angeles, California.

about: Royal Caribbean Cruises is a Miami-based cruise operator, listed on NYSE (RCL), running Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea, with about 65 ships and the world's largest cruise ships (Icon of the Seas). Revenue is around $16 billion with over 6 million guests a year. It sells holidays to consumers worldwide, with its private island Perfect Day at CocoCay. Very high consumer brand awareness, partnering with sports and entertainment properties.

Virgin Voyages is an adults-only cruise line based in Plantation, Florida, launched in 2020 with ships such as Scarlet Lady, Valiant Lady, Resilient Lady and Brilliant Lady, sailing from Miami and Mediterranean ports. Owned by Virgin Group and Bain Capital, it sells cruise holidays to consumers and groups with a focus on dining, wellness and entertainment. Founded 2014. Strong, lifestyle-led consumer brand with celebrity and creative marketing.

wiki.title: Virgin Voyages
wiki.text: Virgin Voyages is a cruise line headquartered in Plantation, Florida and a joint venture between the Virgin Group and Bain Capital.

about: Trip.com Group is a leading online travel company headquartered in Shanghai and listed on Nasdaq (TCOM) and Hong Kong. Brands include Ctrip, Trip.com, Skyscanner and Qunar, offering flights, hotels, rail, packages and corporate travel to hundreds of millions of customers, mostly in China but expanding internationally. Founded 1999. Annual revenue is over 50 billion yuan. Strong consumer brand in Asia and, through Skyscanner, in Europe.

wiki.title: Trip.com Group
wiki.text: Trip.com Group Limited is a multinational travel agency headquartered in Shanghai, China. It was the largest online travel service in the world in 2017.

about: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts is a Toronto-headquartered luxury hotel operator, founded in 1960 by Isadore Sharp, managing over 120 hotels, resorts and branded residences in more than 45 countries, including properties in Paris, New York, Maldives and Dubai. It earns management and licensing fees, and is owned by Cascade Investment (Bill Gates), Kingdom Holding (Prince Alwaleed) and Isadore Sharp. Customers are high-net-worth travellers. Premium global hospitality brand with long record in luxury partnerships.

wiki.title: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts
wiki.text: Four Seasons Hotels Limited, trading as Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts, is a Canadian luxury hotel and resort company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. As of 2026, Four Seasons operates more than 130 hotels and resorts worldwide. Since 2007, Bill Gates and Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal have been majority owners of the company. As of January 2022, Gates-controlled Cascade Investment owns 71.25% and Alwaleed-controlled Kingdom Holding Company owns 23.75% of Four Seasons.

about: Bangkok-based hospitality group, operating hotels under NH, Anantara, Avani, Tivoli and Oaks, with about 560 hotels in 60 countries. Listed in Bangkok as part of Minor International. Known consumer travel brand, especially in Asia and Europe. Minor Hotels is controlled by Minor International and listed in Thailand; it also includes Avani and Oaks, with strong luxury and mid-market hotel recognition.

wiki.title: Minor Hotels
wiki.text: Minor Hotels is an international hotel owner, operator, and investor headquartered in Bangkok, Thailand, with more than 550 hotels in over 55 countries across Asia-Pacific, the Middle East, Africa, the Indian Ocean, Europe, and the Americas. Minor Hotels operates as a subsidiary of Minor International, one of the largest hospitality and leisure companies in the Asia-Pacific region. The group operates hotels under the brands of Anantara Hotels & Resorts, Avani Hotels & Resorts, Elewana Collection, Oaks Hotels, Resorts & Suites, NH Hotels, NH Collection, nhow Hotels, and Tivoli Hotels & Resorts.

about: Hong Kong-based luxury hotel group, founded 1971, operating Shangri-La, Kerry and Traders hotels across Asia, listed in Hong Kong. Strong consumer luxury brand in Asia. Operates about 100 hotels in Asia and beyond. Strong luxury brand with high awareness among travellers. Shangri-La Group is based in Hong Kong and listed there; the Kuok family is the controlling shareholder. The group employs tens of thousands of people and is known for its Shangri-La, Kerry and Traders hotel brands, mostly in Asia.

wiki.title: Shangri-La
wiki.text: Shangri-La is a fictional place in Tibet's Kunlun Mountains, described in the 1933 novel Lost Horizon by the British author James Hilton. Hilton portrays Shangri-La as a mystical, harmonious valley, gently guided from a lamasery, enclosed in the western end of the Kunlun Mountains. In the novel, the people who live in Shangri-La are almost immortal, living hundreds of years beyond the normal lifespan and only very slowly ageing in appearance.

about: Trip.com is a leading Chinese online travel agency, founded as Ctrip in 1999 and renamed Trip.com Group, with Crunchbase listing Singapore for its international brand. It sells flights, hotels, trains, packages and tickets through Trip.com, Ctrip, Skyscanner and Qunar, and is listed on Nasdaq (TCOM) and in Hong Kong. Revenue is above 50 billion yuan. It is a strong consumer brand, and a recognised sponsor of sporting events in Europe and Asia.

wiki.title: Trip.com
wiki.text: Trip.com is an online travel agency headquartered in Singapore, owned by Trip.com Group. Its website and mobile app can be used to book flights, hotels, trains, rental cars, airport rides, tours, attraction tickets, eSIM cards, and more.

about: Qantas is Australia's flag carrier and largest airline, founded in 1920, operating Qantas, QantasLink, Jetstar and Qantas Freight, with a fleet of around 300 aircraft and a Frequent Flyer programme with over 14 million members. Headquartered in Mascot, Sydney, and listed on the ASX (QAN), it has about 25,000 employees and revenue near 20 billion Australian dollars. Very high consumer brand visibility in Australia and the Asia-Pacific, with a flying kangaroo logo; long-term sponsor of Australian sport including the Wallabies and cricket.

wiki.title: Qantas
wiki.text: Qantas Airways Limited, doing business as QANTAS or Qantas, is the flag carrier airline of Australia, and the largest airline by fleet size, international flights, and international destinations in Oceania. A founding member of the Oneworld airline alliance, it is the only airline in the world that flies to all seven continents, with it operating flights to Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, and South America from its hubs in Sydney, Perth, Melbourne, and Brisbane. It also flies 60 to 65 domestic destinations across Australia.

about: Wingstop is a Dallas-based franchisor of fast-casual chicken wing restaurants, with more than 2,500 locations in the US and international markets, known for flavours such as Lemon Pepper and Atomic and for heavy digital ordering. It earns royalties from franchisees, with system-wide sales above 4 billion dollars. Founded in 1994, it listed on Nasdaq in 2015 (WING). High-profile consumer brand and an active marketer with sports tie-ins in the US.

wiki.title: Wingstop
wiki.text: Wingstop Inc. is an American international fast food chain that primarily sells Buffalo wings.

about: TUI Group is the world's largest leisure travel company, headquartered in Hanover, Germany, combining tour operators (TUI), airlines (TUI fly), hotels and resorts (Riu, TUI Blue, Robinson), cruises (TUI Cruises, Marella Cruises, Hapag-Lloyd Cruises) and the TUI Musement activities platform, selling holidays to tens of millions of customers, mainly in Europe. Revenue is roughly 23 billion euros. Listed in London and Frankfurt. Very strong consumer brand in the UK and Germany.

wiki.title: TUI Group
wiki.text: TUI AG is a German multinational leisure, travel and tourism company; it is the largest such company in the world. TUI is an acronym for Touristik Union International. TUI AG was known as Preussag AG until 1997, when the company changed its activities from mining to tourism. It is headquartered in Hanover, Germany, and trading on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange.

about: DraftKings is a US sports betting, iGaming and daily fantasy sports company headquartered in Boston and listed on Nasdaq (DKNG). It operates sportsbook and casino apps in most legal US states and Ontario, plus DraftKings Marketplace and Jackpocket, and has become one of the two market leaders with revenue near 5 billion dollars. Founded 2012. Customers are adult bettors. Very strong consumer brand with large sports league and team sponsorships.

wiki.title: DraftKings
wiki.text: DraftKings Inc. is an American digital sports entertainment gambling company based in Boston, Massachusetts. It offers sportsbook and daily fantasy sports (DFS) services.

about: Aristocrat Technologies is the Sydney-based gaming company behind Aristocrat Leisure, the world's largest slot machine maker alongside IGT and Light and Wonder, with an Australian heritage dating to 1953. It makes casino electronic gaming machines and systems, and owns digital game studios (Product Madness, Big Fish, Plarium) that publish mobile titles such as Lightning Link and Cashman Casino. Customers are casino operators and mobile gamers. Listed on the ASX (ALL) with a market value above A$30 billion. Strong B2B name, growing consumer game reach.

wiki.title: Aristocrat Leisure
wiki.text: Aristocrat Leisure Limited is an Australian gambling machine manufacturer, which has its administrative and research headquarters in the Sydney suburb of North Ryde. It has marketing and development offices in the United Kingdom, Europe and the United States. The company develops and supplies electronic gambling machines, casino management systems, online real-money gambling technology, iLottery products, and social casino games.

about: Superbet is a Bucharest-based gaming and betting group running sports betting, online casino and retail shops in Romania, Poland, Serbia and other markets, with more than a thousand shops. It has been a high-profile sports sponsor, including Romanian football and the Superbet Chess Classic, and also owns the Poland-based Superbet operations. A consumer-facing gambling brand with heavy sports marketing, which matters given restrictions on gambling advertising.
cb_desc: Superbet is an online gaming company in Romania.

about: FDJ is the French national lottery and gaming group, short for Francaise des Jeux, based in Boulogne-Billancourt, operating Loto, Euromillions, scratch games and the Parions Sport betting brand across around 30,000 points of sale and online. It was privatised and listed on Euronext Paris in 2019, with the French state still a significant shareholder, and has since expanded into online betting by buying Kindred in 2024. Revenue is in the billions of euros. Highly recognised in France, and a long-running sports sponsor, including the Groupama-FDJ cycling team.

wiki.title: FDJ United
wiki.what: Operator of the French national lottery
wiki.text: La Française des Jeux is the operator of France's and the Republic of Ireland's national lottery games, and the title sponsor of the FDJ cycling team. The name of the company loosely translates as The French Company of Games. The company was previously owned and operated by the French government. In July 2018, the French government, which owned 72% of FDJ, took the company public and sold off 50% of its ownership to bolster public finances.

about: Swiss sports data and technology firm based in St Gallen supplying live data, odds, and integrity monitoring to sportsbooks and leagues, with rights deals with the NBA, NFL, UEFA and others. Customers include betting operators, media and sports bodies in dozens of countries, with revenue from data feeds, odds services and trading tools plus its Sportradar Integrity Services and Sportradar Ad:s offerings. Nasdaq listed as SRAD since 2021. B2B with strong sports industry presence.

wiki.title: Sportradar
wiki.what: Swiss multinational sports data services company
wiki.text: Sportradar AG is a Switzerland-based sports technology company. The company provides sports data services for national and international sports federations, media outlets, and bookmakers. It also provides streaming media services to several federations and leagues, as well as sports integrity services.

about: LIV Golf is a professional golf league launched in 2022 that is funded by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, with 54-hole team events, big prize money and players such as Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau. Run from the UK and US by Greg Norman as chief and later by Scott O'Neil. Funding shown is about 6.5 billion dollars. Prominent in sports media and a controversy for sportswashing concerns. High sports visibility and an active sponsorship portfolio.

wiki.title: LIV Golf
wiki.text: LIV Golf was a professional golf tour that operated from 2022 to 2026. The name "LIV" referred to the Roman numeral 54, the number of holes that were originally played at LIV events. The first LIV Golf Invitational Series event started on 9 June 2022, at the Centurion Club in England. The Invitational Series became the LIV Golf League in 2023.

about: PureGym is a Leeds-based low-cost gym operator, one of the largest in Europe, with around 600 sites and about 2 million members in the UK, Switzerland, Denmark, Saudi Arabia and Mexico. It earns monthly membership fees, with no contracts, and has expanded via acquisitions including Fitness Park in France. Owned by Leonard Green & Partners after buying it from KKR-backed owners in 2021. Private. Strong UK consumer brand with substantial advertising, including football partnerships.

wiki.title: PureGym
wiki.what: Fitness club chain in the United Kingdom
wiki.text: PureGym Limited is a British chain of no-frills health clubs, with headquarters in Leeds. It is Britain's largest gym chain by membership, with over 1,900,000 members registered to their gyms. PureGym also operate gyms in 8 more countries and have over 500 locations worldwide; the newest territory, the UAE, opened in 2022.

about: Equinox Group is a US luxury fitness company headquartered in New York, operating high-end Equinox clubs, SoulCycle studios, Blink Fitness and the Equinox Hotels brand, with about 100 clubs and premium memberships costing hundreds of dollars a month. It also sells digital fitness and Equinox+ products. Founded 1991, owned by private investors led by Related Companies' Stephen Ross and Vornado. Revenue is about 1 billion dollars. Premium lifestyle consumer brand appealing to affluent urban customers.

wiki.title: Equinox Group
wiki.text: Equinox Holdings, Inc. is an American fitness company and health club headquartered in New York City. The company operates more than 300 club facilities in major cities in the United States, as well as in London, Toronto, and Vancouver in Canada.

about: Real Madrid C.F. is the Spanish football club, member-owned and based in Madrid, 15-time European Cup and Champions League winner and one of the most valuable sports franchises globally, with annual revenue above 1 billion euros. It earns income from matchday, broadcasting, commercial sponsorships and merchandising at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium, plus basketball and other sports. Its global following runs into hundreds of millions; sponsors include Emirates, Adidas and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Very high consumer visibility; already an elite sponsor-seeking property that may compete with F1 for budgets.

wiki.title: Real Madrid CF
wiki.text: Real Madrid Club de Fútbol is a Spanish professional association football club based in Madrid. The club competes in La Liga, the top tier of Spanish football.

about: Chelsea Football Club is the London Premier League club, based at Stamford Bridge, with two Champions League titles (2012, 2021) and a Club World Cup in 2025. It has been owned since 2022 by the BlueCo consortium led by Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital. Revenue comes from broadcasting, matchday and commercial sponsorship, including deals with Nike, Infinite Athlete and Chelsea's women's team. Revenue is about 500 million pounds. Huge global fan base and an elite sports sponsorship property.

wiki.title: Chelsea F.C.
wiki.what: Association football club in London, England
wiki.text: Chelsea Football Club is a professional association football club based in Fulham, West London, England. They compete in the Premier League, the top tier of English football, and rank among the most successful clubs in English football history. The club was founded in 1905, taking its name from the adjacent area of Chelsea, and plays its home matches at Stamford Bridge. Domestically, the club has secured six top flight league titles, eight FA Cups, five League Cups, four FA Community Shields, and two Full Members' Cups. Internationally, their honours include two UEFA Champions Leagues, two UEFA Europa Leagues, two UEFA Cup Winners' Cups, two

about: Italian football club based in Milan, FC Internazionale Milano, founded in 1908, a Serie A champion and 2023 and 2025 Champions League finalist. Owned by US fund Oaktree after Suning Holdings defaulted in 2024. Sponsors include Pirelli and Emirates. Global fan following and strong sponsorship visibility.

wiki.title: Inter Milan
wiki.text: Football Club Internazionale Milano, widely referred to as Internazionale or simply Inter, and commonly known as Inter Milan in English-speaking countries, is an Italian professional football club based in Milan, Lombardy. Inter is the only team to have an unbroken presence in the top division of Italian football, currently Serie A, since its debut in 1909, having never been relegated to Serie B. Since 1947, Inter has shared the San Siro stadium, the largest stadium in Italy, with AC Milan, with whom it contests the long-standing Derby della Madonnina, one of the most widely followed rivalries in world football.

about: FC Bayern Munchen is Germany's most successful football club, based in Munich, with over 30 Bundesliga titles, six European Cup/Champions League wins, and revenue around 1 billion euros. Members own most of the club, with Adidas, Audi and Allianz holding stakes in the football AG. Major sponsors include Deutsche Telekom, Qatar Airways (until 2023) and Emirates. A global sports brand with hundreds of millions of fans, itself a sports property.

wiki.title: FC Bayern Munich
wiki.text: Fußball-Club Bayern München e. V., commonly known as Bayern Munich, FC Bayern or simply Bayern, is a professional sports club based in Munich, Germany. They are most known for their men's professional football team, who play in the Bundesliga, the top tier of the German football league system. Bayern are the most successful club in German football and are among the world's most decorated, having won a record 35 national titles, including eleven consecutive titles from 2013 to 2023 and a record 21 national cups, the DFB-Pokal, alongside one of the highest number of top European titles.

about: Sotheby's is one of the world's oldest and largest fine art and luxury auction houses, founded in London in 1744 and now headquartered in New York. It runs auctions and private sales of art, jewellery, watches, wine, cars and real estate (Sotheby's International Realty, now a separate franchise brand). Customers are wealthy collectors. It was taken private in 2019 by Patrick Drahi's BidFair/Altice-linked interests, and later partnered with ADIA. Very high prestige brand among affluent consumers.

wiki.title: Sotheby's
wiki.text: Sotheby's is a British multinational corporation with headquarters in New York City. It is one of the world's oldest and largest brokers of fine and decorative art, jewellery, and collectibles. It has 80 locations in 40 countries, and maintains a significant presence in the UK.

about: Umicore is a Belgian materials technology and recycling group, making battery materials for electric vehicles, catalysts for car emissions, and recycled precious metals, with revenue of several billion euros and roughly 11,000 employees. Founded in 1805 and headquartered in Brussels, it is listed on Euronext Brussels (UMI). Customers are car makers and battery producers. B2B with a limited consumer profile.

wiki.title: Umicore
wiki.text: Umicore N.V., known as Union Minière before 2001, is a Belgian multinational materials technology company headquartered in Brussels, Belgium.

about: Alpargatas is a Brazilian footwear company based in São Paulo, owner of the Havaianas flip-flop brand sold in more than 100 countries, plus Osklen and previously Mizuno and Topper. Listed on B3 (ALPA3), controlled by Itaúsa and Cambuhy. Revenue is around R$ 5 billion. Very strong consumer brand, with Havaianas known globally and with a history of sport and lifestyle marketing.

wiki.title: Espadrille
wiki.what: Casual shoe with a rope sole
wiki.text: Espadrilles are casual shoes with soles made of esparto rope. The upper is usually canvas or cotton fabric and can vary widely in style. They are usually flat but sometimes high-heeled.

about: Orkla is a Norwegian branded consumer goods group based in Oslo, listed on Oslo Bors (ORK). Its businesses cover packaged foods (Orkla Foods, with Felix, Grandiosa, Abba, Beauvais and Ma Baker), confectionery and snacks (Nidar, Olw, Estrella), home and personal care (Pierre Robert, Jordan), health and sports nutrition, and Orkla Health and Orkla Food Ingredients. Revenue is near NOK 60 billion, with operations across the Nordics, Baltics and India. Very strong Nordic household brand portfolio and a major sports and events sponsor in Norway.

Dream Games is an Istanbul mobile game studio, founded in 2019, best known for Royal Match, a match-3 puzzle game that is among the top-grossing mobile games worldwide. It earns from in-app purchases and advertising from tens of millions of players globally. Reported annual revenue exceeds $1bn. Backed by Index Ventures, Makers Fund and others, it raised $255m in 2021 and was valued near $2.75bn; Savvy Games Group (Saudi PIF) acquired it in 2023 for about $4.9bn. Consumer game brand with heavy advertising in many countries, which includes TV and sports.

wiki.title: Royal Match
wiki.text: Royal Match is a casual free-to-play tile-matching video game launched in 2021. It was developed and published by Dream Games. In it, players follow the fictional King Robert as he restores and refurbishes his castle. The game runs on the Unity game engine and is available for iOS through the App Store and Android via Google Play, the Amazon Appstore, and the Galaxy Store. Since 2023, Royal Match has been amongst the top ten largest mobile games by monthly revenue globally. There are about 55 million monthly active users.

about: Entain is a London-based global sports betting and gaming group, with brands including Ladbrokes, Coral, bwin, Sportingbet, Eurobet, PartyCasino and a 50 percent stake in BetMGM in the US, plus Gala Bingo and TAB in Australia. It operates in many regulated markets, with revenue near GBP 5bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (ENT), formerly GVC Holdings. Strong consumer brands, with a heavy football and sports marketing record; regulation limits motorsport tie-ups in some markets.

wiki.title: Entain
wiki.text: Entain plc, formerly GVC Holdings, is an international sports betting and gambling company. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange, trading under the ticker LON:ENT, and is a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index. It owns brands such as bwin, Coral, Ladbrokes, PartyPoker, and Sportingbet.

about: Vantage Studios is a subsidiary of Ubisoft, formed in 2025 with Tencent investing EUR 1.16bn for a 25 percent stake, based in Montreuil near Paris, to operate the Assassin's Creed, Far Cry and Rainbow Six franchises. It sells games to consumers through digital and retail and earns subscription and live-service revenue. Controlled by Ubisoft (Euronext: UBI) with Tencent as a minority holder. Strong consumer franchise brands, though Vantage as a corporate name is new.

wiki.title: List of Ubisoft subsidiaries
wiki.text: Ubisoft is a French video game publisher headquartered in Montreuil, founded in March 1986 by the Guillemot brothers. Since its establishment, Ubisoft has become one of the largest video game publishers, and it has the largest in-house development team, with more than 20,000 employees working in over 45 studios as of May 2021.

about: Light and Wonder is a Las Vegas gaming technology company that makes slot machines, casino management systems, table games and iGaming content, plus the SciPlay social casino unit that it has since sold. It supplies casinos and online operators globally, earning product sales and gaming revenue shares, with revenue near $3.2bn. Formerly Scientific Games, it listed on Nasdaq (LNW). B2B brand known in casinos, not by consumers.

wiki.title: Light & Wonder
wiki.what: American electronic gaming and gambling company
wiki.text: Light & Wonder, Inc., formerly Scientific Games Corporation (SG), is an American corporation that provides gambling products and services. The company is headquartered in Enterprise, Nevada, with a Las Vegas mailing address.

about: Fanatics is a US sports merchandise and fan engagement company headquartered in New York, selling licensed jerseys, apparel and collectibles for the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, football clubs and others through its online stores and partner sites. It also operates Fanatics Collectibles (Topps), Fanatics Betting and Gaming, and Fanatics Fest, with a valuation of roughly 31 billion dollars in its 2022 round. Customers are fans and leagues, and it earns from merchandise sales and licensing. Privately held. Very strong consumer sports brand already working with F1 teams and leagues.

wiki.title: Fanaticism
wiki.text: Fanaticism is a belief or behavior involving uncritical zeal or an obsessive enthusiasm. The political theorist Zachary R. Goldsmith provides a "cluster account" of the concept of fanaticism, identifying ten main attributes that, in various combinations, constitute it: messianism, inappropriate relationship to reason (irrationality), an embrace of abstraction, a desire for novelty, the pursuit of perfection, an opposition to limits, the embrace of violence, absolute certitude, excessive passion, and an attractiveness to intellectuals.

wiki.title: Fanatics, Inc.
wiki.text: Fanatics, Inc. is an American sports platform that consists of several businesses, including licensed sports merchandise, trading cards and collectibles, sports betting, special events, and live commerce. The company was founded in Jacksonville, Florida, by Michael Rubin in 2011 as an online retailer of licensed sportswear and merchandise for major collegiate and professional sports leagues and teams.

about: Epic Games is a US video game and software company headquartered in Cary, North Carolina, creator of Fortnite, the Unreal Engine game engine, the Epic Games Store and Fall Guys. It serves hundreds of millions of players and developers, earning from in-game purchases, engine royalties and store fees. Founded 1991 by Tim Sweeney; Tencent holds a large minority stake and Sony and Disney have invested. Huge consumer brand with extensive brand and sports partnerships in Fortnite.

wiki.title: Epic Games
wiki.text: Epic Games, Inc. is an American video game and software developer and publisher based in Cary, North Carolina. The company was founded by Tim Sweeney as Potomac Computer Systems in 1991, originally located in his parents' house in Potomac, Maryland. Following its first commercial video game release, ZZT (1991), the company became Epic MegaGames, Inc. in early 1992 and brought on Mark Rein, who has been its vice president since. After moving the headquarters to Cary in 1999, the studio changed its name to Epic Games.

about: Square Enix is a Japanese video game and entertainment company, whose parent Square Enix Holdings is in Tokyo and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (9684); Crunchbase records its London office. It publishes Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest, Kingdom Hearts and many other franchises, plus manga, and earlier owned Western studios such as Eidos, which it sold to Embracer in 2022. Revenue is from games, mobile titles and licensing. Globally recognised games brand, popular with younger consumers.

wiki.title: Square Enix
wiki.text: Square Enix Holdings Co., Ltd. is a Japanese multinational holding company, video game developer, publisher, and entertainment conglomerate. It releases role-playing game franchises, such as Final Fantasy, Kingdom Hearts, and Dragon Quest among numerous others. Outside of video game publishing and development, it is also in the business of merchandise, arcade facilities, and manga publication under its Gangan Comics brand.

about: Nexon is a Japanese video game company, whose parent Nexon Co. is in Tokyo and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (3659), with Nexon America located in El Segundo, California per Crunchbase. It operates online games including MapleStory, Dungeon & Fighter, FC Online, Blue Archive and The First Descendant. Revenue is from in-game purchases, mostly in Korea, China, Japan and North America. Global games brand with strong recognition among online gamers.

wiki.title: Nexon
wiki.text: Nexon Co., Ltd. is a South Korean–Japanese video game developer and publisher specializing in live service games. It develops and publishes titles including MapleStory, Crazyracing Kartrider, Sudden Attack, Dungeon & Fighter, The First Descendant, and Blue Archive. Headquartered in Japan, the company has offices in South Korea, the United States, Taiwan, and Thailand.

about: Hybe is a South Korean entertainment company based in Seoul, founded as Big Hit Entertainment and best known as the agency for BTS, with labels including Pledis (Seventeen), Source Music, Belift Lab and Ador (NewJeans), plus the Weverse fan platform and gaming and education businesses. It earns revenue from music, concerts, merchandise and fan membership. Listed on the Korea Exchange (352820) since 2020, it has a global fanbase and strong consumer brand visibility, especially among younger audiences.

wiki.title: Hybe
wiki.text: Hybe Co., Ltd., commonly known as simply Hybe, is a South Korean multinational conglomerate. Founded as Big Hit Entertainment, Hybe has grown from a traditional music entertainment company into a tech-driven lifestyle platform corporation.

about: Electric vehicle and clean energy company selling the Model S, 3, X, Y and Cybertruck, plus Powerwall and Megapack storage, solar products, the Supercharger network and autonomy software (Full Self-Driving, robotaxi and Optimus robot efforts). Sells directly to consumers and utilities online and via company stores, with roughly 1.6 to 1.8 million vehicles delivered yearly and over 120,000 employees. Headquartered in Austin, Texas; founded 2003, led by Elon Musk. Listed on Nasdaq (TSLA). Globally famous, no traditional advertising or sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Tesla, Inc.
wiki.what: American electric vehicle and clean energy company
wiki.text: Tesla, Inc. is an American multinational automotive and clean energy company. Headquartered in Austin, Texas, it designs, manufactures, and sells battery electric vehicles (BEVs), stationary battery energy storage devices from home to grid-scale, solar panels and solar shingles, and related products and services.

about: Online local commerce platform connecting consumers with restaurants, grocery and retail stores for delivery and pickup, including DoorDash Dashpass and the Wolt service in Europe after the 2022 acquisition. Earns commissions and fees from merchants, consumers and advertising, and uses a network of independent couriers (Dashers). Headquartered in San Francisco, California; founded 2013. Listed on Nasdaq (DASH), operating in the United States, Canada, Australia, Japan and Europe with revenue around 10 to 12 billion dollars. High-visibility consumer app brand and a major advertiser.

wiki.title: DoorDash
wiki.text: DoorDash, Inc. is an American company operating online food ordering and food delivery. It trades under the symbol DASH. With a 56% market share, DoorDash is the largest food delivery platform in the United States. It also has a 60% market share in the convenience delivery category. As of December 31, 2020, the platform was used by 450,000 merchants, 20 million consumers, and had over one million delivery couriers.

about: Medical technology company making imaging equipment (MRI, CT, ultrasound, X-ray), patient monitoring, diagnostics, pharmaceutical diagnostics contrast agents and digital health software. Customers are hospitals, clinics and healthcare systems worldwide; revenue around 20 billion dollars and approximately 50,000 employees. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois; spun out of General Electric in January 2023 and listed on Nasdaq (GEHC). B2B healthcare brand with solid recognition among clinicians and little consumer-level visibility.

wiki.title: GE HealthCare
wiki.text: GE Healthcare Technologies, Inc., stylized GE HealthCare, is an American health technology company based in Chicago, Illinois. It operates four divisions: Medical imaging, which includes molecular imaging, computed tomography, magnetic resonance, women’s health screening and X-ray systems; ultrasound; Patient Care Solutions, which is focused on remote patient monitoring, anesthesia and respiratory care, diagnostic cardiology, and infant care; and Pharmaceutical Diagnostics, which manufactures contrast agents and radiopharmaceuticals.

about: One of China's largest e-commerce companies, selling electronics, appliances, groceries and general merchandise with its own logistics network, plus JD Health, JD Logistics and JD Industrials. Operates a direct retail model and third-party marketplace, serving hundreds of millions of Chinese consumers and businesses with annual revenue above 150 billion dollars. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 1998 by Richard Liu. Listed on Nasdaq (JD) and in Hong Kong (9618). Very strong consumer brand in China, with limited recognition elsewhere though it is expanding in Europe.

wiki.title: JD.com
wiki.text: JD.com, Inc., also known as Jingdong Group, formerly called 360buy, is a Chinese multinational technology company specializing in e-commerce, retail, Internet, and technology. The company is headquartered in Beijing. With revenues more than US194 billion in 2025, JD.com is China's largest retailer by revenue, and ranks 47 on Fortune Global 500. It is one of the two massive B2C online retailers in China by transaction volume and revenue, and is a major competitor to Alibaba-run Tmall. JD.com's portfolio spans across retail, technology, logistics, health care, industrials, property management, private label, insurance, and international busines
